note: All target entities are synthetic (see synthetic-catalog-adversarial-v1.json). 'tag: baseline' means the query matches a registered alias already in the catalog - should already pass. 'tag: stress' means the query is deliberately NOT a registered alias - this is the real test of fuzzy/phonetic generalization. See README.md.

scenarios.rationale: Exactly matches the one alias that IS registered on this record.
Common alternate English romanization of a Russian-origin given name, deliberately not registered as an alias. Tests phonetic/fuzzy generalization, not alias lookup.

Fully anglicized given-name form. Harder than translit-02 - tests whether matching goes beyond edit-distance/phonetic folding into known cross-language name equivalence, which most systems (including this one, on current evidence) do not attempt. Expect this one to fail; that's useful information, not a bug to panic over.
Exactly matches the registered alias.
Single-M spelling plus al-/el- prefix substitution, common real-world variance in Arabic-origin name romanization. Not registered.
Prefix merged into surname with no hyphen or space at all - tests tokenization robustness, not just spelling tolerance.
No ASCII-folded alias is registered at all on this record - purely tests whether the normalizer strips diacritics before comparison, or requires an exact accented-character match.
Mixed - one accent kept, one dropped. Simulates realistic manual data entry rather than a clean full-fold or full-original.
Third word order for this name (primary is CHEN WEI EXAMPLE, registered alias is EXAMPLE CHEN WEI) - neither the primary name nor the registered alias uses this order. Tests token-order independence.
Surname-first-with-comma convention common in some vendor data feeds.
Legal-entity suffix (LLC) dropped entirely - extremely common in free-text payment fields.

Catalog record itself has no DOB on file; query also supplies none. Tests matching on name alone when no corroborating identifier exists on either side - and whether the system can express appropriately lower confidence rather than a false full-confidence exact match.

Initials-only queries are inherently ambiguous (many people share 'M. Novak'). The correct behavior is NOT a confident auto-match or auto-clear - it's routing to human review. A system that returns high-confidence auto-match here is arguably worse than one that fails to match at all, because it will generate false confidence at scale.

Query identifier is a truncated prefix of the real passport number (EX1234567). Tests whether the system correctly avoids treating a partial-prefix identifier match as strong corroborating evidence (it shouldn't - prefix collisions are common) while still catching the name-level match.
Name cut off mid-word, simulating a field-length-limited upstream system. Tests prefix/truncation tolerance.

Leading 'O' replaced with visually identical Cyrillic 'О' (U+041E). Renders identically in most UIs but is a different Unicode codepoint. This is a well-known real evasion technique (homoglyph substitution) and, based on the normalization code reviewed, is very likely NOT currently handled - the normalizer only does whitespace/casing, no Unicode confusable folding. Expect this to fail; treat that as the single highest-priority finding from this whole test bank.
Digit zero substituted for letter O (plain ASCII, not a homoglyph) - tests fuzzy edit-distance rather than Unicode folding specifically.
Same digit-substitution pattern against the original base-catalog entity.
Zero-width space (U+200B) inserted mid-word - invisible in most UIs, present in the underlying string. Tests whether normalization strips non-printing Unicode, not just visible whitespace.
Excess punctuation - very common in real free-text payment fields, low-effort but high-frequency noise.
Full token reordering, no other change.
Single-character edit distance (S -> Z), plausible as an innocent typo or a deliberate near-miss.

Corporate suffix swapped (GMBH -> LTD), same core name, implying a different jurisdiction/entity type. This mirrors a real sanctions-evasion pattern: re-registering the same operation under a new corporate wrapper. High-value test.

Singular 'Holding' vs the catalog's 'ORION HOLDINGS GMBH' and 'ORION TRADING GMBH' - one edit away from two different real entities. Correct behavior is surfacing both as candidates for human disambiguation, not silently picking one with high confidence.
Added honorific prefix and generational suffix, hyphen dropped from al-Exampli. Tests whether added tokens dilute the match score below threshold.

Three plausible-but-fake middle names inserted, deliberately designed to dilute a token-overlap-based score below a naive threshold. Tests resistance to a padding/dilution evasion attempt specifically, not just tolerance of noise.

Simulates an upstream integration bug (not deliberate evasion): the entire name crammed into a single field. Tests robustness to malformed upstream input, which is at least as common in production as deliberate adversarial behavior.

known_status_note: known_status reflects an actual run against the compiled adversarial.owpcat package via matcherbaseline on 2026-07-30. pass/fail are regression-checked by internal/adversarialtest; ambiguous_as_expected and unscored are logged but not asserted as pass/fail.
